text: Streaming was implemented during the "efficiency-driven" phase of the education system in the 1980s and 1990s.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: We were concerned about the huge number of dropouts who could not read or write at the end of primary school.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: We had to move away from a one-size-fits-all education system because if students sat in class, could not catch up, and did not understand their lessons, they would lose interest and drop out.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: The introduction of the N(T) stream contributed significantly to this outcome.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Till today, we are benefiting from the legacy of the "efficiency-driven" education system.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: I urge Members not to casually juxtapose social stratification with streaming because, without reducing attrition rates through streaming, social stratification would have been far, far worse.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Over time, parents and students also began to see the benefit of learning at a pace and rigour suited to their academic abilities.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Today, for students whose PSLE scores allow them a choice between two streams, there are many who, in fact, prefer a stream where they can study at a more comfortable pace, and gain confidence as they feel that they are a "bigger fish in a smaller pond".

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: There is always some margin of error, especially if streaming is done at a young age.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Further, in its original form, streaming assumed that students needed a certain pace of learning in all their subjects, whereas many students, in fact, have uneven strengths across different subjects.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Students can develop a mindset where they tell themselves, "I am only a Normal stream student and this is as good as I can be." It becomes self-fulfilling.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: We have been grappling with this tradeoff between customisation of education and the downside of stigmatisation.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: That is why, over the years, we have made significant changes to the streaming system.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: A major transition took place in the mid-2000s, when MOE phased out streaming in primary school over a period of four years.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: As Members would recall, we used to have three streams in primary school – EM1, EM2 and EM3.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: The first step was to merge EM1 and EM2, since the only difference between the two streams was the standard of MTL.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Later, MOE shifted to customising learning not at the stream level, but at the subject level.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: We introduced different standards for the subjects – Standard and Foundation for English, Mathematics and Science; Higher, Standard, and Foundation for MTL.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: We called this Subject-Based Banding (SBB) and started it since the mid-2000s.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Hence, by 2008, instead of having three streams, we had a single primary school course.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Within the course, students could learn subjects at different standards, based on SBB.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: There were sceptics at that time who asked, "What is the difference between streaming and SBB?

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: It is old wine in a new bottle, that is, 换汤不换药 – you merely changed the labels of EM1, 2, 3 to new subject labels called Foundation, Standard and Higher, that is all.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: It is the same!" There is a big difference.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Streaming separates education into different courses and we put students into each course.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: You put all kinds of cookies into the jar and then you close it, and you label it "pineapple tarts".

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: So, all the goodies inside, whatever they are, get labelled as "pineapple tarts", accurately or inaccurately.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Essentially, we break the jar, students come out of it, take subjects of varying difficulty, based on their academic ability.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Taking one or two subjects at the Foundation level is not tantamount to labelling the child.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: And equally important, it encourages students to find their strengths.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Since we introduced SBB, many students who would previously have been in the EM3 stream ended up taking one or more subjects at a higher level.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: So, this way, we continued to reap the benefits of customisation of education but minimised the downsides of labelling.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: This is much harder to do for secondary school, because there are so many more subjects involved.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: More than a decade ago, we started a form of SBB in secondary schools by allowing students in the N(A) and N(T) streams to take up to two subjects at a higher level starting from Secondary 3, if they had done well in those subjects when they were in lower secondary.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: N(A) and N(T) students in lower secondary could take English, MTL, Mathematics and Science at a more rigorous standard, if their PSLE scores or school examination results for these subjects justified it.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: The results of this new pilot have been encouraging.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: If we break down this number, 25% of N(A) students took one Express level subject; another 11% took two subjects, and over 10% took three subjects or were laterally transferred to Express stream.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: So, 25% plus 11% plus 10%, adding up to roughly half of the N(A) students.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: If we had included MTL, the numbers would be even higher.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: The numbers for N(T) students taking N(A) subjects are also largely similar.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: As of now, the two batches of students who have participated in SBB in the prototype schools have completed their secondary school national examinations.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: To illustrate, for the national examinations in 2018 last year, 25% of Secondary 4 N(A) students who took GCE "O" level English got A1 or A2.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: For GCE "O" level Mathematics, 26% of N(A) students got A1 or A2; Express students, 50%.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: For GCE "O" level Combined Science, it was N(A) students, 33%; Express students, 34%.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: I think the Normal stream students have held their own.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Our surveys also showed that students, parents and teachers overwhelmingly welcome this.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: We are now ready to take a further, major move.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: It will involve a few significant policy steps over the next few years.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: There will be two important milestones – 2020 and 2024.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: How is Full SBB different from vanilla SBB today?

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: First, we will allow lower secondary school students to study more subjects at a higher level – not just English, MTL, Maths and Science today, but also Geography, History and Literature.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Chemistry and Biology will only be available in upper secondary.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: As it may be difficult to ascertain the level suitable for students using just their PSLE results, MOE and schools will develop guidelines and assessment mechanisms, including using Secondary 1 year-end examinations.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Express students today are already exposed to technical subjects, such as Design and Technology.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: In time, Express students may take subjects offered in the Normal stream, such as Mobile Robotics.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: The third big difference, beyond the academic aspects, Full SBB will also give pilot schools an opportunity to reshape the social environment in schools to benefit their students.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Day-to-day practices in schools play a big part in shaping a child's self-confidence, sometimes more than the academic curriculum.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: I learnt this from Mr Tan Chor Pang, the principal of Boon Lay Secondary.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: The late-coming and absenteeism rates amongst Normal stream students in Boon Lay Secondary had not been healthy.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: However, Chor Pang observed that when it came to CCA, all the students were very engaged.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: So, in an unprecedented move, he figured, let us just change the way we organise classes.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: I was fascinated by this unorthodox practice and decided to visit the school and speak to teachers and students.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: I found out that, every morning, students would gather in their CCA groups – which is their form class – for morning assembly.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: They also underwent Character and Citizenship Education classes and learning journeys together as a form class based on CCA.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: For academic lessons, they then break out into different classes based on SBB.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: So, I asked the students: "Why the big reduction in late-coming and absenteeism rates when the principal changed the class organisation?" The students were frank.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: They told me that many of them had personal and other family problems.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Teachers and counsellors could help, but they also needed peer support, especially from their seniors and friends in their CCA.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Now, they look forward to attending morning assembly, because this is when they meet their friends and seniors from their CCA groups.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: One student told me: “Now I can pour my heart out to my seniors every morning before assembly, even if it is for 10 minutes.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: But to do so, I must come to school and come on time.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: In fact, 10 minutes earlier!” Another Normal stream student told me something quite profound.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: He said that in the past, during morning assembly, a teacher might admonish a noisy class and say: "4N(T), keep quiet!" Immediately, all the N(T) students felt that they were singled out.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Today, the teacher would say: "NCC, keep quiet!" and the Normal stream students feel: "Okay lah." The students who have gone through almost two years of the new form classes in Boon Lay Secondary have recently completed their national examinations.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: MOE will need to study their results further, but there is now a genuine belief that the social environment of the school can positively influence a student’s academic behaviour and performance.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: I also visited another school, Edgefield Secondary, which had decided to reorganise form classes to include students from all three streams starting this year, not by CCA, but mixed form classes with students from all three streams.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Each Secondary 1 form class goes through about half of their lessons together, for subjects like Character and Citizenship Education (CCE), Design and Technology, Art, Music and Physical Education, where there is little need to customise lessons based on academic abilities.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: The other half, comprising academic subjects – English, MTL, Maths and Science – are grouped according to SBB.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: It has only been a couple of months, but feedback has been generally good.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: The students I spoke to have no basis for comparison, so they all say it is very good, and they are very happy, as expected.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: The teachers noticed that students were helping one another more frequently in class, and students from the Normal stream were stepping forward to take up leadership roles during group work or project/team work.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: I chatted with several students at the canteen.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: I asked them, "You all think this is great.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: But how about your parents?" They said their parents felt it was okay.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: One student said "My father thought 'This is Awesome'." The principal, Mr Lee Peck Ping, told me that a handful of parents were concerned that this might slow down learning in class.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Peck Ping painstakingly explained how SBB worked, what students are learning together as a form class, and how classes for academic subjects are still banded based on the learning abilities of the students.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Through this explanation, he managed to address the concerns of most parents.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: He told me that a small number of parents were still worried and felt that, had they known, they would not have sent their children to Edgefield Secondary.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: And I understand the concerns of these parents.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: But Edgefield Secondary was making the right tradeoff to develop students both academically and socially.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: It was, in its own way, taking the lead in reshaping our existing culture for the better.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Schools, such as Boon Lay and Edgefield, are important trailblazers and I thank them.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: We should not underestimate the challenge of this move.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: There are major operational challenges, such as timetabling.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Schools will need time to learn, adapt and innovate.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: By the start of 2024, we will be ready to take the next step, which is the most crucial.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: One, we would have rolled out Full SBB and the new ways of organising form classes across the education system.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: The pioneering practices in Boon Lay and Edgefield will become the norm.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: It will list the subjects completed and the standard band of each subject, very much like what Dr Intan Mokhtar described yesterday.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: And we are not unfamiliar with this concept.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: It is actually similar to the GCE "A" level certificate for JCs, where the certificate states the subjects and the standards they are completed in, whether it is H1, H2 or H3.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Singapore and Cambridge will co-brand this new certificate.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: We are both strong international brand names in education and, by working together, we will enhance the recognition and value of the certificate.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: With Full SBB implemented, form classes reorganised across the board, and a combined secondary school education certificate, we would have effectively merged Express, N(A) and N(T) into a single course.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: So, from three education streams, we will now have "one secondary education, many subject bands." We will no longer have fishes swimming down three separate streams.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: We will have one broad river, with each fish negotiating its own journey.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: I am sure that there are many questions on how all this will work.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Some of them will need to be addressed as we implement the changes.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: But let me answer a few key ones.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: An immediate question is whether we will still keep Secondary 5.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: It is a key concern amongst students and parents, because for N(A) students today, attaining the GCE "O" level through Secondary 5 helps them to access the polytechnics and JCs.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Our plan is that by 2024, all students will enrol into Secondary 1 and go through a four-year curriculum for all subject bands.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: At the end of Secondary 4, these students will attain the common certificate with various subject permutations.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Some will have six G3 subjects and one G2 subject; some will have five G3s and two G2s; others, maybe two G3s, three G2s and one G1 and so on.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: This will require us to undertake a review of our post-secondary posting system, so that students taking a combination of G1, G2 and G3 subjects can be fairly considered for ITE, polytechnic and JC.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Our review will recognise students’ particular strengths that make them suitable for specific post-secondary courses.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: The year 2024 is a few years away, and we will use this time to undertake this review.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: We will also explore other alternatives to a fifth year in secondary school, like the current Polytechnic Foundation Programme, to help students bridge over to polytechnic or JC.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Another question is: currently, the great majority of secondary schools admit students from the Express, N(A) and N(T) streams.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: How will the secondary school posting system change?

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: MOE has thought this through and concluded that it is better not to disrupt the current posting system.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: This means that secondary schools should continue to admit students across three PSLE scoring bands, even though the streams have been merged.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Educationally, this approach is both practical, reasonable and sound because the transition from Primary 6 to Secondary 1 is a fairly major one, and a significant one for all students.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: PSLE still serves as a useful initial gauge of the subject bands that each student is most suited for at the beginning of Secondary 1.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: So, students admitted in the first PSLE scoring band will initially take mostly G1 subjects, those in the second PSLE scoring band will take mostly G2 subjects, and those in the third PSLE scoring band will take mostly G3 subjects.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Admitting students across three PSLE score bands will allow schools to offer subjects of all bands.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: But once in secondary school, students can discover and further develop their strengths and interests, and Full SBB will enable them to diverge into various paths, taking a combination of subjects across different bands.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Admitting students from different PSLE scoring bands into the same secondary school will ensure that our students get to make friends from diverse backgrounds.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Indeed, one of the key objectives of education is to forge a cohesive society.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: This leads to the third question, which is, then what will happen to Spectra and Crest, which currently take in only N(T) students, or schools with specialised programmes, such as NUS High School, the School of Science and Technology, and Integrated Programme schools that take in only Express stream students today?

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Will MOE mandate that they take in students across all three PSLE bands?

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: There is value in having certain schools take a whole-school approach in implementing specialised programmes.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Every education system in the world will have schools that cater specifically to different segments of students, such as those with high academic ability and strengths in specific areas or who much prefer a more hands-on, vocational and technical training.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Such a diverse education system can complement the plan to move beyond streaming.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: We should maintain and balance diversity across schools and within a school, to allow us to better cater to the educational needs and strengths of different groups of students.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: The downside is the lack of mixing in these more specialised schools.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: These schools have to make a special effort to recruit students from all backgrounds, wisely using their Direct School Admissions mechanism.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: They will have to ensure that students participate actively in inter-school mixing opportunities, such as combining school CCAs, Outward Bound School camps, or Values-in-Action projects where week-in, week-out, students from different schools get to mingle together.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: I can see many of the principals from the specialised schools working very hard to do better in this aspect.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: There is also scope for these specialised schools to offer more subject options.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: After all, customisation of education and catering more flexibly to the varied interests and abilities of students will benefit them.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: The emphasis of our education system has evolved over the years.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Four decades ago, we made major progress in customising education to reduce student attrition.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: From two decades ago, we have been redesigning the system to develop the varied abilities of our students.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: In the digital era, knowledge has become very accessible.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: One smartphone and you can access all kinds of knowledge.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Skills, both technical and soft, are what make us human and inoculate us from being replaced by computers and robots.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: But skills take a lifetime to acquire and hone, and one must be driven by passion to do so.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: In this phase, more than ever, we are centred on the need to learn for life, to prepare our students for the future.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: We are able to take these steps now because of the work done in the past.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: So, in a way, whatever I have announced could have been anticipated.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: In fact, many Members of Parliament who urged for the phasing out of streaming, made reference to SBB, and saw this as a natural extension of all the work that we have done.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: And this has to be our attitude when it comes to education – never complacent, always anticipating the future, figuring out what needs to change next, planning it out, and implementing at a pace that takes into account the tradeoffs, complexities and the immense impact any changes will have on our students.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: We should never stay frozen for long periods, only to make sudden changes years later.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: So, any change that can be compared to the slaughtering of any animal is probably a bad idea.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: I am confident that "one secondary education, many subject bands" will benefit many students.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: When I was young, the only books I read were Chinese comics.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: I entered Primary 1 not being able to understand English very well, much less reading and writing.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: My late mother, a Chinese teacher, tried to teach me, but her English was also very limited.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Then sometime in Primary 3, I had a eureka moment.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: I figured out that if "b-a-r" reads "bar", "b-e-r" reads "ber", then "b-a-r-b-e-r" – I can put them two together and it becomes "barber" – the guy who cuts my hair!

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: So, I had figured out phonics in Primary 3.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: From then on, I could start to read some English books.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: I could read the words and sentences, but I had a problem because I did not know what they meant.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: So, in secondary school, my English standard was what my classmates would describe as "cannot swim".

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: This affected other language-dependent subjects, such as History and Geography.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: And in the exam, I kept my fingers crossed.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: If I had spotted the exam questions correctly, then I would regurgitate what I had memorised.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: If the exam questions came out wrong, I regurgitated anyway.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: But if I were in primary school today, I would probably have been put into a Learning Support Programme, which would have done me a lot of good.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: I should have done G2 or G1 English.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: There are some students who are very strong in every academic subject.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: But most, like myself, have uneven strengths, and specific weaknesses.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: The challenge of our education system is to cater to that.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: That is the central purpose of this change.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Put to rest the mistaken notion that there is a single, dominant path to success that starts from a very young age.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Beyond schools, the IHL landscape offers even more varied pathways for the student to develop and grow, based on his talents and strengths.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Mr Chairman, several Members have raised the issues of inequality and social mobility.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: As these cuts span the work of several Ministries, they will be addressed in a collective response by myself, Minister of State Zaqy Mohamad, Senior Parliamentary Secretary Sun Xueling and Minister Desmond Lee.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: We will do so by building a society of opportunities for all.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: We will ensure that education continues to be a key lifelong enabler for all to progress, irrespective of starting point or background.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: We will help those in the working world upgrade their skills and learn new ones, so they can access employment opportunities at all stages of life and have good incomes.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: We will support lower-income families in their aspirations towards home ownership and provide extra support for Singaporeans from disadvantaged backgrounds.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: This cannot be achieved by the Government alone.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: It requires a whole-of-society effort, with Government agencies, employers, community, families and individuals working together as one.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: In education, we have built a system where opportunities are available to all.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: We have many schemes to assist disadvantaged students and their families at every stage of education.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: For those who do, the difficulties are real, as highlighted by Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar, Mr Charles Chong, Mr Murali Pillai and Mr Muhamad Faisal Abdul Manap.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: The question then is how we can help them overcome their challenges so that they can benefit from the help that is available and realise their full potential.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: The task force's aim is to deep-dive into problems and issues faced by underperforming students from disadvantaged families, understand what exactly is preventing them from doing better, identify gaps to be filled and devise practical solutions.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: To get to grips with the real issues and causes, the task force has engaged people at the frontline, that is, those who work directly with and are most familiar with the problems faced by disadvantaged families.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: To date, we have engaged over 200 contributors, including school leaders and staff, students, parents, social workers, self-help groups (SHGs), community partners and volunteers.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: First, long-term absenteeism, as mentioned by Miss Cheng Li Hui and Mr Leon Perera.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: However, the numbers, while small, represent a discernible group that needs help.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: The reasons for absenteeism are varied, but most often, it is tied up with complex family issues.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: There are existing efforts to address this issue.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: For the preschool sector, the Early Childhood Development Agency engages some of these families through the KidSTART pilot and Preschool Outreach programme, where the professionals conduct home visits and work with families, including to improve preschool attendance for the children.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: In our schools, we monitor students' attendance closely and actively engage parents when students are absent without reason.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Student Welfare Officers and school counsellors are trained to identify early warning signs and reach out to students who show signs of disengagement from school to provide timely interventions and support.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: However, as the root causes often lie in the family situation, we will have to direct more efforts in that area.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Second, the lack of a structured and supervised environment outside of school.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Typically, when a child comes home after school, there is a proper routine – lunch, some rest, a quiet environment and time set aside for homework, and thereafter play.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: However, many disadvantaged children do not have such an environment at home.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Third, children who underperform due to lack of self-confidence, motivation and resilience.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: These students feel disconnected and isolated from their peers.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Their perception of what they can achieve is constrained by difficult circumstances, and they struggle with self-esteem or other underlying emotional issues that hinder them from doing well.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: In the UPLIFT engagements, my team met Santhya, a student from ITE College Central.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Santhya was disengaged when she first started ITE.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: She became depressed, lacked self-confidence and began having an anxiety disorder.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Her teachers engaged and encouraged her, to build up her self-confidence.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Fortunately, Santhya had the motivation and resilience to overcome her depression and anxiety disorder.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: She did well in her National ITE Certificate (NITEC) course and is now pursuing a Higher NITEC in Engineering with Business.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: She is also part of the Student Council in ITE College Central.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: The question is how we can help others like her find the resilience and motivation to overcome their challenges.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Many parents in the target profile struggle to balance work and caring for their children.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: They love their children but they feel inadequate in their parenting skills and do not know how to establish control or strike the necessary balance.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: They typically also face multiple issues – financial difficulties, split families, unstable housing arrangements and, in some cases, domestic violence or a lack of caregiving for younger and elderly family members, resulting in the older children becoming substitute caregivers and, hence, unable to focus on their education.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: As there are many different aspects to UPLIFT, some initiatives can be done earlier, while others will take more time to develop.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: We will progressively announce the various initiatives as and when they are ready.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: One has already been launched, that was the UPLIFT Scholarship announced by Minister Ong Ye Kung in December 2018.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Today, I would like to announce two more initiatives.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: During my recent visit to the SCC in Lian Hua Primary, I met Syed Al-Hafiz, currently in Primary 5.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: He lives with his elderly grandmother, and his neighbour, Uncle Tan accompanies him and his siblings to school every day because his grandmother is occupied with looking after his younger siblings.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Hafiz initially had trouble adjusting to school and used to misbehave.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Under the care of his teachers, his neighbour Uncle Tan and the SCC staff, Hafiz responded positively.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: The SCC provided Hafiz with a structured after-school environment for him to develop good habits and daily routines.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: He is now doing well and is happy to come to school.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Hafiz's experience shows that community support, coupled with the right care environment and encouragement, can make a big difference.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Given the positive outcomes of MOE's after-school care, we will adopt a three "E" approach.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: We will expand current provisions, increase enrolment, and enhance programmes to strengthen motivational support, resilience and holistic development.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: There are currently 170 SCCs in primary schools.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: With increased SCC capacity, we can take in more children.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Schools will, therefore, make a more concerted effort to reach out to parents whose children would benefit from attending SCCs, especially those with no alternative care arrangements, and facilitate their enrolment.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: We are studying the difficulties that disadvantaged families may face in enrolling their children into SCCs.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: One issue highlighted in our engagement is the affordability of student care for low-income families.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Today, children from low-income families attending registered SCCs receive subsidies for their SCC fees through the Student Care Fee Assistance scheme.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Nonetheless, some students on MOE's Financial Assistance Scheme could still have to pay more than $100 per month.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Many primary schools work with their SCC vendors to take full advantage of the after-school hours to develop their SCC students holistically, for example, through enrichment and character-building activities.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Parents and students have given positive feedback about such programmes.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: We will continue to build on these efforts and will introduce additional programmes aimed at strengthening students' resilience and improving their socio-emotional well-being.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: As Miss Cheng Li Hui mentioned, the transition from primary to secondary school has to be smooth, especially for disadvantaged students.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Currently, primary school counsellors or Allied Educators (AEDs) share transition support strategies with parents, as well as information of students with higher needs with their secondary school counterparts.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: The secondary schools then ensure continuity of financial support, provide academic bridging and extend other forms of additional support to those who need it.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Since 2014, secondary schools have piloted after-school programmes for students who need more support and supervision.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: The schools provide a room for the students, which they can use for self-study and various activities after school.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: The activities and programmes could be run by teachers, community partners or volunteers.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Students are also mentored by teachers and external youth workers.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: These programmes have strengthened socio-emotional support to students and improved their connectedness to their learning, peers and school.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Greendale Secondary School was among the 60 secondary schools that piloted after-school programmes, with very encouraging results.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: They adopted The Scaffold Programme (TSP) in 2016, in partnership with SHINE Children and Youth Services.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: One Greendale student who benefited from TSP was Fida'iy.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Fida'iy displayed anger management issues at first and was disruptive in class.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: His family was also going through difficult times.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: After attending TSP's programmes, and with guidance and counselling from his youth worker, Jie Xi, Fida'iy learnt to manage his emotions better.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: He developed a good relationship with Jie Xi, who was also in regular contact with his family to help create a supportive and conducive home environment.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Fida'iy is now a positive influence in class.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Through GEAR-UP, schools will work with community partners to provide customised support and after-school engagement and strengthen our students’ socio-emotional competencies and social skills.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: These programmes will be especially helpful to students from disadvantaged families, who will benefit from customised support and care.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: The issues faced by disadvantaged students are multifaceted, and not all the interventions or assistance can or should be school-based.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Many other Government agencies also provide assistance, as do community-based organisations, such as the SHGs, grassroots organisations, voluntary welfare organisations (VWOs) and individual volunteers.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Community partners play a crucial role in uplifting our students.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: They offer a range of services to support children and youths from disadvantaged families, such as after-school care and support within the community and programmes to build students' motivation and resilience.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Ulu Pandan Stars Programme is another volunteer-driven initiative which mobilises more than 100 secondary to tertiary student volunteers to provide academic coaching and mentorship to over 70 students from disadvantaged families in Ghim Moh.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: The programme engages and involves parents in the learning process and collaborates with schools to support students' learning needs.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: One clear theme that has emerged from all the engagement sessions is the need for better coordination to tap community efforts and resources more systematically.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Ms Tan Bee Keow and Ms Joy Lim of the Singapore Children's Society said that the locale-based engagement sessions gave them a clearer sense of local needs and a more complete picture of the programmes by other community partners in the same neighbourhood.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: They expressed a wish for a more coordinated approach among agencies to ensure that the children’s needs are well met and there is no duplication of services.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: MSF is taking steps to strengthen social service delivery and coordination amongst agencies and community partners.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: MOE is also supporting MSF's efforts to tighten local coordination among schools, SSOs, FSCs, other community organisations and VWOs.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: This involves strengthening outreach and case management for families which need it, for example, by improving data sharing and coordination of complex cases.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: It will help in a number of ways.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: First, it will work with schools to identify disadvantaged students and map their needs, to facilitate community-based outreach to the families, and matching to suitable community programmes or assistance.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Second, to help schools better leverage community assets and volunteer networks to support after-school activities or holiday programmes for these students, UPO will match trusted partners and volunteers to schools, working with the SSOs and SG Cares Community Network, as well as tap on retired educators who wish to volunteer.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: In the first instance, UPO will focus on supporting school-community coordination in selected pilot sites which have higher numbers of students and families fitting the target profile.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: UPLIFT has other initiatives in the pipeline, but this will get us off to a good start.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Zhi Xian struggled with low self-esteem when he joined Assumption Pathway School (APS).

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Compounded with family and financial issues, he became rebellious and disruptive.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Zhi Xian's teachers supported him through counselling and constant encouragement.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: He was paired to cook with his teacher during certain culinary classes.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: This allowed the teacher to directly mentor and encourage him.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: He slowly built up his motivation and self-esteem and became more confident.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: He was part of the school team that won the bronze medal in a culinary competition.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: He also started counselling and mentoring his peers.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Zhi Xian went on to clinch the 2018 Award for Best Culinary Skills student in APS.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: He is currently enrolled in ITE's NITEC in Asian Culinary Skills and continues to strive hard and give his best.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: For us, every child is precious and we want each and every one of them to achieve his or her fullest potential.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: This is especially so in the case of those from disadvantaged backgrounds, since they face more challenges than others.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Together, we can build a society of opportunities where every Singaporean can do well, succeed and progress, irrespective of background.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Earlier, Minister Indranee Rajah has shared about MOE's effort to ensure that every child has a start in life to fulfil his or her aspirations.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: I shall now touch on how we uplift Singaporean workers.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: The outcomes, if we look at the handout, show that we are moving in the right direction.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Individual income growth also translated into increased household incomes.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Significantly, the employment rate for residents remained high at about 80% even as income grew.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: But these outcomes did not happen by chance.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: They arose from multiple layers of support to upskill our workers, uplift their wages, while keeping unemployment low and employment high.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: What this means is that we must stay focused on three key strategies.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: First, we must maintain a thriving economy with a tight labour market and constantly look out for opportunities to create better jobs.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Full employment is the best way to ensure the welfare of our workers.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Next, we must strive for quality growth based on productivity improvements that all Singaporeans can benefit from, including our lower-income workers.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Third, we support our lower-income workers at both the broad-based level and within specific sectors so that they can progress with the rest of the workforce.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: My speech today will focus on this third thrust.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: MOM will elaborate on the first two thrusts during our Committee of Supply (COS) debate later.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: The WIS scheme is a broad-based measure that tops up the salaries of our lower-income workers and helps them save for retirement.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Sixty-four-year-old Mdm Goh Geok Kee will be one such beneficiary.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Auntie Geok shared with me that she has been cleaning our MOM Service Centre and receiving WIS for the past seven years.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: With this year’s WIS enhancements, Auntie Geok's WIS payouts will boost her income by about 25%.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Auntie Geok told me that as long as she remains fit, she would like to continue working.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Mr Zainal Sapari suggested removing the age differentiation for WIS.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: We designed WIS for more payouts to go to older workers like Auntie Geok who have less runway to upgrade their skills and save for retirement.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: We hope to encourage more older workers like Auntie Geok to be more economically active.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Our younger workers have greater potential for income growth and can be better supported through upskilling efforts to improve their human capital.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: WIS also helps workers save more for retirement.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Mr Zainal Sapari proposed increasing the cash component from 40% to 80% and decreasing the CPF component from 60% to 20%.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: The cash component today is, in fact, higher than when WIS first started.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: In addition, whenever the Government provides extra WIS bonuses, such as this year’s WIS Bicentennial Bonus, these bonuses are generally paid fully in cash.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: I understand Members' desire to look after the workers' immediate needs.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: From 2020, the enhanced WIS payouts will give all workers higher cash payments for daily needs.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: We worry about how they will cope when they eventually stop work.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: We also want our lower-income workers to benefit from the higher interest earned in CPF.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Compounded over time, the savings will help them have more in retirement.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: We will also help the workers who need financial assistance, through ComCare and other schemes.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: We will continue to review WIS regularly to help target groups like Auntie Geok and her co-workers.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Most WIS recipients, including Auntie Geok, also receive other Government support to help meet their living needs.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Over 90% of our WIS recipients receive U-Save rebates and additional cash assistance under the Goods and Services Tax (GST) Voucher scheme.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Four in 10 receive medical and dental subsidies under the Community Health Assist Scheme (CHAS).

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Those with children also receive childcare and student care subsidies, if eligible.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Nearly half receive three or more types of Government transfers each year.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Notably, 75% of our WIS recipients own their homes.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: I think this is a very laudable statistic to remember.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Forty-nine-year-old Mr Gunasegaran s/o Sellayya is another good example.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Mr Guna works as a supervisor, managing eight other cleaners.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: GST Vouchers and U-Save rebates help to offset his daily household expenses.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Mr Guna owns a three-room flat that he lives in with his family.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: His two elder daughters receive MOE Financial Assistance.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Each gets a waiver of standard miscellaneous fees, free textbooks and school attire, and public transport credit.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: His youngest son receives the Kindergarten Financial Assistance.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Mr Guna enjoys 99% of kindergarten fee assistance, paying only $1 monthly for kindergarten.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Mr Guna's retired mother also has a CHAS Orange card and receives subsidised care at CHAS clinics.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: So, Mr Chairman, our approach of providing multi-layered support is more responsive to the varied needs of our lower-income individuals than any single minimum wage or living wage.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Importantly, we achieve significantly faster real median income growth, and ranked high on employment rates, compared to other developed countries.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Beyond transfers, we also support skills upgrading to help lower-income workers achieve sustainable wage growth, and progress along with the workforce.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: The WIS Training Support Scheme encourages lower-income workers to upskill to access better jobs with higher wages as the economy transforms.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: The tripartite partners have introduced the Progressive Wage Model (PWM) in the Security, Landscape and Cleaning sectors as a targeted intervention to address the market failure of “cheap sourcing” and support sustainable wage increases.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Since implementation, workers in these three sectors have seen positive real wage growth.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Dr Intan Mokhtar asked whether PWM can be extended to more sectors.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Ultimately, improving productivity is key to sustainable wage growth.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: We also encourage employers in other sectors to adopt the principles of progressive wages and skills and provide clear progression pathways for their workers.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: On a voluntary basis, employers and unions have also established PWMs in public transport and healthcare.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: We will explore facilitating more of such voluntary PWMs.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Mr Zainal Sapari suggested reviewing the PWM training requirements to specify compulsory modules.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: As Chairman of the three Tripartite clusters, the Member would be aware that the tripartite partners have agreed on the training requirements in the PWMs, including specifying mandatory modules and giving employers flexibility to send their workers for other relevant training.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: We have also been enhancing these three PWMs with wage enhancements and bonuses.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Together, the tripartite partners are fully committed to improving the lives of our lower-income workers.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Beyond improving wages, MOM also works closely with our tripartite partners to improve our workers’ well-being.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: I will cover this in MOM's COS debate.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Mr Chairman, we have had a decade of WIS.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: The handout highlights key outcomes of WIS, and how WIS and the multiple layers of support have uplifted families like Mr Guna’s and Auntie Geok's.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: We achieved good income growth while keeping employment high.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Our lower-income workers continue to upskill and, as I mentioned earlier on, looking at home ownership, they also continue to grow their assets.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Let us build on what is working well for Singapore and stay on the task of uplifting Singaporean workers like Auntie Geok and Mr Guna.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Mr Chairman, I will speak on home ownership, which is central to providing stability and progress for families in the long run.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Home ownership gives Singaporeans a stake in our country, and gives each family a permanent place to call their own.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Also, households can use their CPF to pay for their mortgage, giving them a home and an asset, instead of using cash to pay rent.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: That said, some families run into difficulties, such as job losses, and are unable to own a home for some time.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: We work closely with MSF to ensure that they are not left without a roof over their heads.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Those who lack family support and alternative housing options will be assisted with public rental housing.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Members have asked how we help tenants to attain home ownership.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: We agree that public rental should only be temporary for tenants who are work-capable and are, therefore, increasing support to help tenants progress towards home ownership.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Beyond direct financial assistance, we seek to ensure that the families can sustain home ownership independently.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: We also work with MSF to check in with the families regularly to ensure that the family situation remains stable.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: These numbers may seem small, but for those who benefit from the scheme, the help provided means a lot and we want them to succeed in their home ownership journey.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: This is why we regularly review ways to enhance Fresh Start and to intensify support for those who are already on the scheme.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: I will share more details on these enhancements at MND's COS.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Through Fresh Start, we have gained a better understanding of how best to support our tenants in their journey towards home ownership.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: For example, some needed advice on budgeting for a flat purchase.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Others shared that they appreciated the face-to-face support from the Fresh Start team.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: As Members can imagine, it is a manpower-intensive effort, but such individualised efforts are well worth it.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: We want to provide stronger, personalised handholding for families which are ready for home ownership.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: HST will help tenants navigate home ownership policies and processes, from discussing the options that would best meet their needs and budget, guiding them through the purchase, and checking in to ensure that the family remains on track for key collection.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: We have learnt that having someone to consult and, more importantly, to provide the human touch, is important for our tenants.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: HST will be set up later this year and will start reaching out to families with potential for home ownership.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Home ownership may not be an immediate goal for some tenants who may first need to address more complex challenges, such as family conflict.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Our priority is to help these families stabilise.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Hence, we will be providing spaces for MSF to establish social service hubs near rental flats to offer localised programmes and services.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Once these families have stabilised, we look forward to engaging them for HDB to work with them on their journey towards home ownership.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: I have met many rental tenants who aspire towards home ownership.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: These numbers have increased steadily in the last few years.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: We want to keep this up and will work hard to partner our tenants in their efforts.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: (In Mandarin):   Home ownership allows every Singaporean to live and work with peace of mind and to grow with the nation.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: In spite of this, there are families that face difficulties in life, such as unemployment, and are unable to afford their own flat.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Members have asked how we can help households living in rental flats to buy their own homes.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: We will continue these efforts and do more to help rental flat tenants own their homes.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: We noticed that some tenants in rental flats require budgeting advice when buying their own flat, some are grateful for the face-to-face counselling and assistance provided.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: I am glad to announce that HDB will establish HST, which is a dedicated team to help tenants in rental flats kickstart the process for home ownership.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: First of all, HST will help tenants understand the policies and processes of buying a flat and discuss suitable options for them after considering their needs and budget.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: HST will provide guidance through the process of the flat purchase and ensure that everything proceeds smoothly, up to the collection of keys.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: We realised that having someone to provide information and advice and, more importantly, the human touch, is very important for these residents.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Before buying the flat, some families would need to resolve complex challenges, such as family disputes.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Mr Chairman, may I have your permission to present two slides in the course of my presentation and also a little bit more time to complete this joint segment.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Mr Chairman, my colleagues have described some of the further measures that we will take to give our children a good start, uplift our workers and support families living in rental housing.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: I will update Members on our efforts to provide stronger and more integrated support for Singaporeans with complex challenges.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: These include enhancements to ComCare, setting up of Community Link (ComLink) for families in rental flats and Localised Community Networks to support youths-at-risk.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: ComCare is a key component of our social safety net.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: It complements the support provided by family, community and other Government assistance.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: We regularly review our ComCare schemes at MSF, with inputs from our stakeholders.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: ComCare Long-Term Assistance (LTA) supports those who are permanently unable to work due to old age, illness or disability and have little or no income and family support.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Most of our beneficiaries are elderly Singaporeans and they receive monthly cash assistance for living expenses and household bills; assistance with medical bills, medical consumables and one-off essentials; and access to Government-funded social services, such as Senior Activity Centres and befriending services, to stay engaged and connected.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Over the last 10 years, MSF has reviewed and adjusted these rates every two or three years.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: In addition to ComCare LTA, the Government has enhanced wraparound support for seniors in recent years, so that our seniors can age with better assurance.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Members will see a picture of Mdm Jaya, pictured here together with Priya from SSO@Hougang and Moses from Fei Yue Cluster Support.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Since 2016, she has been receiving ComCare LTA cash assistance.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Sunlove Home Help delivers meals to her every day, as part of the Ministry of Health's Meals-on-Wheels programme.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: She receives cash supplements through the Silver Support Scheme and we assist her with her medical bills and medical consumables.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: She further benefits from the Pioneer Generation Package, which provides additional help with her healthcare costs.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Fei Yue Cluster Support officers also visit her every year to check on her well-being and we hope such wraparound support will help Madam Jaya and seniors like her live and age well in their golden years.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: For example, those whose breadwinners are temporarily unable to work, looking for job or earning a low income may receive temporary support through SMTA.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Amounts will vary depending on their needs and financial circumstances.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: These are part of our efforts to strengthen social assistance for the vulnerable, which Dr Lily Neo and Mr Seah Kian Peng asked about.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Beyond enhancing our social assistance schemes, we must continue to strengthen the ways in which families receive help.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Families facing complex situations often require support beyond financial assistance.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: And it can be challenging for them to navigate the system and interface with multiple agencies and VWOs.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: To achieve better sustained outcomes, we are working to provide more Comprehensive, Convenient and Coordinated assistance, and I will share more at MSF's COS.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: I will move on to the second significant area of strengthened support which concerns rental families.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Senior Parliamentary Secretary Ms Sun Xueling had earlier described some of MND's efforts to help families living in rental flats.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: We will also do more to enhance support holistically for these families and, in particular, work with a network of partners to help them and their children overcome early disadvantages and do better as they grow up.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: In July last year I sketched out plans to set up social service hubs at or near rental flats.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Dr Lily Neo and Mr Seah Kian Peng have asked about our plans and, over the past few months, we have been consulting our partners.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: MSF, together with MND, will be launching ComLink at or near rental flats to offer more integrated and coordinated support and customised programmes and services for families living there.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: ComLink will provide an accessible focal point in each community.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: The SSO and officers from other social services will work together and proactively support those in need.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Community partners can also come together to assist these families more holistically through ComLink.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: For example, we may bring in parenting workshops and night-time student care or childcare, if such needs are identified in the community.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: We chose these sites because of their profile of rental families with children.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: At each of these sites, dedicated spaces will be available for community partners to run programmes catering to the needs of the families.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: This is a photo of one of the programmes provided at the existing space in Jalan Kukoh which we are using.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: ComLink will provide proactive, collaborative and community-driven support to these families.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
