text: The SSOs have brought community partners like the grassroots, Government agencies on the ground and VWOs together in local implementation workgroups to better understand each community's specific needs.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: These implementation workgroups will be engaging the families and the local community to better understand their aspirations and their needs.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: We want to design programmes and services alongside them.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: And we look forward to working with partners to serve the community.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Apart from families living in rental housing, we also look into the needs of children and young people who may be derailed because of family issues, such as financial difficulties or family conflict.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Their parents may also be absent or unable to care for them.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: These are stressful situations that can affect the children, including the level of motivation and learning in school, which Minister Indranee Rajah has been looking into under UPLIFT.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Without proactive early support and intervention, some of these students may underperform or start to skip school.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Yet, these are young people with potential and promise, and we want to ensure that they have the best chances in life.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: By facilitating fuller data sharing between the relevant Government agencies, we hope to gain a better understanding of the challenges they face at home, in school or elsewhere.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: And in doing so, we hope to help them resolve or cope with the issues they are facing.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: The pilot also complements UPLIFT's efforts to support students who exhibit long-term absenteeism or emerging attendance issues arising from challenging family circumstances.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: ComLink and the Localised Community Network pilot are part of our efforts to strengthen the way in which families receive help, and strengthen the overall social service network.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: The Government will continue to invest in and strengthen our system of social support.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: But with the needs of families becoming more complex, it is encouraging to see more community organisations and volunteers joining us in our efforts to uplift families.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: To ensure that such goodwill and resources translate into a more impactful and sustainable improvement, we must work together to organise and integrate our community efforts better.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Mr Chairman, over the past year, public consciousness about the challenges of income inequality and social mobility has been raised through a series of thoughtful books, articles, forums and programmes.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: These include Channel NewsAsia’s documentary entitled, "Regardless of Class" narrated by Dr Janil Puthucheary; books by academics, such as Assoc Prof Teo You Yenn's "This is what Inequality Looks Like"; and the volume edited by Prof David Chan on "How Working Together Matters"; the dialogue with Prof Tommy Koh and Deputy Prime Minister Tharman Shanmugaratnam at last year's Institute of Policy Studies Conference; and subsequent dialogues involving Prof Tommy Koh and Mr Lim Boon Heng on minimum wage; op-eds by practitioners, policymakers and academics, such as Dr Sudha Nair, Senior Minister of State Maliki Osman and Assoc Prof Walter Theseira, to name a few, and forum letters by members of the public.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Mr Mohamed Irshad asked for the Government’s views on the positions taken in Prof David Chan's and Prof Teo You Yenn's books and, I presume, by extension, the views on inequality articulated by other academics and commentators in the media.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: This is not quite the right platform for a full exposition and assessment of the broad range of issues raised.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: The Government has, in fact, set out its views and approach on inequality and social mobility earlier, in particular, in the Prime Minister's Parliamentary reply, Deputy Prime Minister Tharman Shanmugaratnam's interview with the Straits Times, and MSF's Occasional Paper entitled "Improving the Lives of Low-Income and Vulnerable Families in Singapore".

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: So, let me make a few broad points to close this joint segment.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: First, we welcome the diversity of views and ideas on inequality and social mobility.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: It gives us the opportunity to see fresh perspectives, step back and challenge our own assumptions, so that we can continue to make our system better.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: It also focuses and asks on how each of us can play our part to help uplift Singaporeans in need.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Second, we are encouraged that many more people are volunteering and giving generously.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: More companies are asking how their giving can be made more impactful as we can achieve greater impact if we can better harness our collective resources and complement one another's efforts.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Because there are multiple causes, our solutions must be multifaceted.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Where mindset and motivation are an issue, our social workers seek to counsel, nudge and inspire.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Where life circumstances derail and anchor people down, we try to intervene where possible upstream, to help to solve these difficulties and challenges in their way.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: And where complex and interlocking problems consume a family's attention and ability to access opportunities or respond positively to social interventions, we find ways to strengthen and integrate our social support for them.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: We will keep studying fresh ideas and approaches, both here and abroad.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: We do not assume we have all the answers.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: And few, if any, policies come without tradeoffs or unintended consequences.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: When new ideas or philosophies are offered, we need to see how they have worked in other societies and carefully consider the fuller implications and tradeoffs, so that good intentions do not lead to counter-productive results.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Mr Chairman, the important work of building a society of opportunities for all extends well beyond our four Ministries, to the whole of society and to all Singaporeans.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: In fact, if Members listen throughout the COS, Members will find that in many Ministries, there will be schemes and programmes, thoughts and ideas that they will implement that address the issue of inequality and social mobility.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: None of us got to where we are today on our own efforts alone.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Along the way, we were offered opportunities, second chances or a helping hand.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Our society is stronger and more resilient when all Singaporeans come together and we look out not only for ourselves, but for our families, neighbours and fellow Singaporeans in need.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: And as we do this, we ensure that all Singaporeans have the chance to pursue their dreams, regardless of their background and starting points.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: And this is the society of opportunities that we aspire towards.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: Chairman, I want to direct my questions to MOE.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: I want to thank Minister Ong Ye Kung for finally slaying the sacred cow of streaming, and, of course, not without very good prior examination.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: The Minister might not want to call it "cow", but I would just call it that.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: I wonder if the Minister can comment if that is also a feature that can be examined and then relooked at.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: I think there is just merit to having students who are gifted academically to also mix with students who are taking subjects at G1 or the former Normal level.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: I believe it makes for very good social mixing.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: I wonder if the Minister can consider that as well.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: I truly appreciate what the Minister has shared.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: I know that in MOE, from the Director down to the AEDs, they have done a lot of work, and I want to honour what they do as well.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: Also, to look at a proper skills-based training roadmap for them, because to deal with so many types of disabilities and that kind of numbers is really not easy.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: And at the IHL level, because they are all quite autonomous, for the Ministry to consider resourcing and supporting them through a common platform where they can get together to share best processes and practices in order to make the efforts more effective and impactful.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: So, just like SBB that I mentioned earlier, they spend 50% of the curriculum time together for various subjects.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: Only when it comes to Mathematics, Science, English and Social Studies, they then break out into their GEP classes.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: This is exactly the same balance that we are trying to optimise and we will continue to work on that.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Mr Chairman, I thank Ms Denise Phua for her clarification.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: What I can say to Ms Denise Phua is that we will continue to do more to see how we can support the students with special educational needs (SEN) in our schools.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: It is not just a question obviously of the AEDs but also the teachers, the peers and building up an environment that is generally supportive.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: So, we have made quite a lot of headway in the last few years, and we will continue to do so, and we will certainly take the Member's suggestions into consideration.

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Mr Chairman, I have two clarifications, one for each Minister.

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
text: First, for Minister Ong, I also spoke about the School of the Arts (SOTA) and the Sports School.

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Since we will eventually abolish academic streams by 2024, will there be plans to eventually take students beyond just the Express stream for both SOTA and the Sports School?

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
text: The second question is on Crest and Spectra.

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Eventually, is there still relevance for Crest and Spectra to just have N(T) students?

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Will they be absorbed as a mainstream school, where they can admit students from across all abilities?

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
text: For Minister Indranee, just a couple of questions on SENs.

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Are there plans to let all pre-service teaching programmes in the National Institute of Education (NIE) to also include at least one module on teaching students with special needs?

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Because at this moment, I think only specific groups of pre-service teachers are trained to teach students with special needs.

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
text: So, will there be plans to let all pre-service teachers be trained to manage students with special needs?

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
text: And beyond just resources that are under teaching or schools, what about increasing awareness amongst students themselves?

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Are there plans to include awareness about students with special needs in common subjects for all students, for example, in Character and Citizenship Education lessons, so that they know how to manage classmates who have special needs?

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: SOTA takes in Express stream students plus those in the Option Band where they can opt for both Express as well as N(A).

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: And the reason is because SOTA offers an International Baccalaureate (IB) programme.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: However, in time to come, when the three streams are merged, I think it will naturally have to relook at what kind of students it takes.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: As for Spectra and Crest, as I mentioned in my speech, speaking to Spectra's and Crest's students, they feel so much better being in a school where there is a whole-school approach to recognise that they are probably better at doing technical jobs, hands-on jobs, and develop them in that direction.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: So, there is value to have diversity across schools, having schools that focus on certain segments of students but, at the same time, the bulk in the middle have diversity within the school, which is what we are trying to achieve.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Dr Intan Mokhtar asked about what we are doing to equip teachers to deal with students with special needs.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: There is training for basic awareness for SEN.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: This enables the teachers to understand and manage the learning demands for students with SEN.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: And we also have teachers who are trained in special needs.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: And as of July 2018, 512 teachers have been trained under the revised TSN programme, and some of these TSNs go on to acquire deeper knowledge in SEN support by attending disability-specific training modules.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: With regard to peers, the Member is correct.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: You do want the other students to be empathetic to students with SEN and generally know how to relate to them.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: When I visited some of the IHLs and spoke to some of the students with SEN, they mentioned that when they were younger, they were often misunderstood.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Their peers did not talk to them, would not sit down and interact with them.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: And I think that really did have an impact on them.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: But helping students to understand what it is to be a friend to someone with SEN makes a huge difference.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: And it is not a one-way thing; it is two ways because the child without SEN is also learning what it is like and receives knowledge that way as well.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: So, we will continue to work on that to make sure that their peers interact well with them.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: Mr Chairman, my questions are directed to the Minister for Social and Family Development, Mr Desmond Lee.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: First, I welcome the changes to the ComCare assistance schemes for the short-term, medium-term as well as long-term.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: I note that this is part of regular reviews which the Ministry conducts.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: And, in this instance, it is quite a hefty jump, up to about 20%.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: So, my question to the Minister is whether these reviews could be undertaken more frequently and the adjustments be more incremental but do it more regularly.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: My second supplementary question is: when the Minister spoke about how the Government is helping Singaporeans in the area of social mobility and inequality, the Minister mentioned that they are starting some pilots together with MND, by launching community links at or near rental flats, to offer more integrated and coordinated support and customised programmes and services for families living there.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: First, how will community links support the families within the neighbourhood?

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: And, Mr Chairman, if I can speak on your behalf, I note one of them is in your constituency.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: I have articulated that ComLink, as a social service hub embedded at or near rental housing, will to be able to tackle and address the challenges that rental-housing families face.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Look at each family's circumstances, starting with families with young children; understanding their needs holistically rather than looking at the issues they face.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: So, look at the individual, look at the family, understand what are the challenges that hold them back, that hold them down.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: What are the risks that poverty gets transmitted to the next generation, and the next generation?

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: And work with relevant Government agencies, work with the families, understand what their dreams and aspirations are; work with community partners who will come into ComLink and integrate our support for these families.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: And, of course, work with the neighbours, because they are not beneficiaries and clients, they are people living there, who have abilities, leadership and initiative, and who themselves may have found ways to improve their lot in life.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: And then they can share examples, support one another.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: ComLink is an example of how we want our future of social service integration to be – working together, looking at families holistically rather than individual needs, looking at the whole rather than in silos and compartments.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: I will speak more about that by way of an update during MSF's COS.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: In essence, Members asked how the ComLink approach can benefit the wider neighbourhood.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: An integrated approach to tackling complex challenges in order to achieve maximum social uplift for these families is the way we want to go.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: In terms of corporates and partners, the ComLink white spaces or community spaces will be places which community partners who wish to see their giving achieve maximum impact, they can go there.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: They can say, "I would like to support these families and not just give generally.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: I want to see outcomes, I want to see upliftment in these households.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: I want my colleagues, my staff, my vendors to partner these families, walk the journey with them until some of them have a better life ahead of them to look forward to".

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: So, ComLink is not just a Government initiative.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: It is a platform that allows the broader community to come in – companies, philanthropists, donors, volunteers, givers – but working together in an impactful way, in an integrated and coordinated manner to uplift people's lives.

speaker: The Chairman
text: A reminder to Members to direct more of the questions related to the Ministries subsequently during their COS.

speaker: Dr Lily Neo (Jalan Besar)
text: Mr Chairman, I would like to have two supplementary questions, one for Minister Indranee Rajah, the other for Minister Desmond Lee.

speaker: Dr Lily Neo (Jalan Besar)
text: For Minister Indranee Rajah, earlier on she mentioned on the expansion of after-school care.

speaker: Dr Lily Neo (Jalan Besar)
text: CATCH Plus stands for Children and Teens Community Hub started since 2014 at Kreta Ayer precincts, that is, at the Jalan Kukoh rental blocks.

speaker: Dr Lily Neo (Jalan Besar)
text: It is a holistic care programme for the disadvantaged children there, with a membership of 100 right now.

speaker: Dr Lily Neo (Jalan Besar)
text: So, could MOE help with that one and maybe take over the CATCH Plus Centre?

speaker: Dr Lily Neo (Jalan Besar)
text: For Minister Desmond Lee, on ComLink, may I ask what kind of outreach will there be, because that is most important as the core success for this project?

speaker: Dr Lily Neo (Jalan Besar)
text: Will there will be enough social workers that can have a handholding approach to all these disadvantaged families with multifaceted problems, and also if we can have a long-term basis approach for the children of such families?

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Maybe I can outline what the thinking of the philosophy behind UPLIFT is, and then I will address the question.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: There are some things that should be done in the school within curriculum time by teachers.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Then there is something that can be done in the school but not part of the curriculum, and not necessarily by teachers.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: So, that is what the expansion of SCCs is about.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Then, you have things which are in the community and, for that, there is actually a value to having community-based programmes, because not everybody may want to send their children to an SCC.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: As Members know, when you live in a rental block, sometimes the parents work shift hours, they prefer their children to be at home at a certain time; they cannot collect them from school.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: So, we would like to encourage VWOs, as well as grassroots organisations and other community projects, to continue.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: The question is how to link them up.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: I visited the Member's constituency and I was introduced to the ReadAble Programme.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: I was very impressed by the work that they are doing there, and there is value in that.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: So, it would not be so much a situation of MOE taking over community programmes like that, but what MOE and the UPLIFT office can do, together with MSF, is see how we can link up, coordinate better.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: If programmes like that need assistance or support, we will see how we can connect you with the entities or persons who can better support such programmes.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Chairman, I thank the Member for her question.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: If I may just venture an additional reply on the CATCH Plus programme.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: The Member had also described to me in detail how CATCH Plus works.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: It is where the ComLink for Jalan Kukoh will operate.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Certainly, we will work very closely with the people working in CATCH Plus, to ensure a more integrated support for young people living in rental housing, that particular group that we are very focused on.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: I have spoken earlier about the Local Community Network (LCN).

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: We are starting off a pilot in Boon Lay because we have ComLink there as well.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: But you begin to see how our structures that we will start to put on to the ground begin to relate to one another and work with one another.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: So, the UPO, the LCN support in the schools, we identify younger people who may have difficulties.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Often, you find the challenges begin at home, or the derailers come from beyond them, from the family.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: So, it is not something you can just tackle in school, you really need to work together with the social workers, the family members, siblings and the local community there, to provide that scaffolding and support, so that the young person can thrive and not have his promise snubbed out.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: In terms of ComLink outreach, as I said earlier, rental housing should not just be a promise of infrastructure and shelter.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: It is a shelter where you have no home and it comes with social support.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: That is why, initially, we call it a social hub; rental housing combined with social services, and social services being proactive, integrated, at your doorstep; a journey of social workers and community services with these families when they are at their lowest point in life.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: So, ComLink will build an understanding of the families living in the estate that they serve.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: It is a composite picture that we need to put together with all our partners.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: This also involves outreach to these families, starting with families with young children, understanding their situation, understanding, very importantly, what their dreams are for themselves and, in particular, for their children.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: That was what the Senior Minister of State Maliki Osman found in Project 4650 when Promoting Alternatives to Violence (PAVE) and many other community groups worked together, conferenced monthly, to understand the challenges and dreams of each and every one of the families they serve, until they see light at the end of the tunnel.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: It may take months, years or a very long time to happen.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: But that kind of support, integrated, interlocking, will make a difference.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: So, in terms of outreach, it will be proactive, it will reach out to these families and seek their participation and partnership along this journey.

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
text: Chairman, I agree completely with the Minister for Education that a good AU is one that suits students and develop their full potential.

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
text: So, to support that goal, I would like to ask the Ministry if we can have a commitment to at least study resource-sharing for library materials, as I had raised, because the disparity in access can have serious consequences for learning and for scholarship.

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
text: It also may be cheaper for us to study sharing library resources across the AUs that may allow for economies of scale and bargaining, for example, with the publishers.

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
text: I do have colleagues who actually use their alumni library accounts from their PhD-granting institutions in order to get access to certain library materials.

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
text: They find this easier than trying to rely on their own institutions' resources, and I think we have to fix this problem.

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong
text: Mr Chairman, I thank Senior Parliamentary Secretary Faishal Ibrahim for giving a direct response to my cut.

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong
text: I have two clarifications, one to the Senior Parliamentary Secretary and the other to Minister Ong, please.

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong
text: The first is that I absolutely agree about the programmes that you have started to support the psychosocial well-being of our students.

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong
text: We all agree that there is no health without mental health.

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong
text: I also agree that mental health is complex and multifaceted and, therefore, there is not one clear solution.

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong
text: But I wonder if a good way to start is to reframe the way we see health education in schools.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: Indeed, we look at mental health as something that we want, to build the socio-emotional competency of our children, as well as build the resilience in the programmes that they undertake.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: So, in essence, we start at a very early stage of their education at primary school level, whereby all these values, experiences and components where a child can develop himself or herself emotionally, socially and that resilience in all the programmes that we undertake.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: We take on an approach of prevention, early detection and intervention.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: Of course, we also engage the parents along the way.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: Many of our schools have Peer Support Programmes.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: We see the benefits of having peers looking out for one another.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: I, for one, have come across situations whereby peers were supporting one another, peers informing the educators about some of the issues faced by their own classmates, and the issues are being resolved not only by one person but together as a community.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: So, as I have said earlier, it takes a many-hands approach whereby we want to see how we can enhance the education journey of a child, regardless of where they come from and regardless of the experience that they have, so that they continue to be socially and emotionally resilient and able to have a fulfilling and meaningful educational journey here in Singapore.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: I think there is no disagreement that mental health is part of health, together with physical health.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: In fact, when we speak with students today, teenage students, mental health is one of the top concerns on their mind.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: Definitely, this is something we have to look into and continue to improve.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: What I want to seek the understanding of Members is that the mode of delivery does not always have to be in a curriculum, and under "lessons" and under " talks", taking up curriculum time.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: In fact, for mental health education to really work, it has to be delivered in a different way, such as through peer support groups that Senior Parliamentary Secretary Muhamad Faisal Ibrahim talked about, and also general public education which students now receive through their social media channels.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: So, let us explore different ways and not always channel through the formal MOE education curriculum.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Chairman, my clarification question is with regard to my ITE cuts and I am glad that the Minister mentioned in his speech that all ITE students are not disadvantaged.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: In relation to my cut, it is with regard to the resources at ITE in general, whether there will be more focus on providing enhanced resources to ITE, particularly for SEN students, like what some of the other Members have mentioned as well.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: The second question I have is in relation to my second cut on the ITE question which is about the Joint Admissions process for polytechnics and JCs.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Currently, for ITE students, they apply for the JPAE after all the GCE "O" level students have actually applied.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: In my cut, I actually highlighted whether there will be any tweaks to the process to ensure that ITE students are not disadvantaged in the sense that they only come in after the remaining seats have already been occupied by GCE "O" level students.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: So, may I get the clarification from Minister, please?

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: Look at ITE Ang Mo Kio (Central) – very nice premises.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: So, subsidies for ITE students are much higher compared to polytechnics or universities.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: Thirdly, we continue to build new pathways for ITE students and, one of them, which I explained, was the Work-Learn Technical Diploma, which will be a major programme coming out of ITE.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: So, really, no worries about ITE not resourced enough.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: As for the other question on JPAE, I addressed it in my speech.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: So, they will not be disadvantaged in any way.

text: Ms Denise Phua, would you like to withdraw your amendment?
